parameter_mapping: Recurrent weight W=I; activation f(c)=c+eta c(1-c)(c-a) followed by clip; input embedding U[:,x]=eta(A_x*1 + B_x*(2p-1)); readout projection [M,H]=diag(ell)[1, 2p-1]^T c, then quadratic score with R. Cleavage is disabled by tau->1/2.
update: u_i = clip(c_i + eta*[c_i(1-c_i)(c_i-a) + A_x + B_x(2p_i-1)]) with the partition P frozen (no cleavage), c <- u

comparator: fixed-weight Elman RNN, W=I_2, U=pulse table, activation u - sigma*E_kappa(u)(1,1), read sigma*E_kappa(u_t)
base_form: Elman RNN h_t = f(W h_{t-1} + U e_{v_t}), y_t = g(h_t), with fixed weights and a fixed activation (Elman 1990)
parameter_mapping: hidden state h_t <- x_t = (a_t, b_t); W <- I_2; U <- pulse table w (V x 2); activation f <- pulse-equilibrate-withdraw map with constants (kappa, sigma); readout g <- harvest sigma * E_kappa
update: u_t = I x_{t-1} + w^T e_{v_t}; x_t = f(u_t) = u_t - sigma * E_kappa(u_t) * (1,1), with E_kappa(u) = 2 u_A u_B / (u_A + u_B + kappa + sqrt((u_A - u_B)^2 + 2 kappa (u_A + u_B) + kappa^2))

comparator: Elman RNN in rotated basis (d,s)=(b-a,a+b) with E_kappa(S,D)=(S+kappa-sqrt(D^2+2kappa S+kappa^2))/2
base_form: Elman RNN with a fixed activation, written in a rotated basis (Elman 1990)
parameter_mapping: d <- b - a; s <- a + b; per-token input (beta_v - alpha_v, p_v = alpha_v + beta_v) <- rotated pulse table; kappa and sigma unchanged
update: d_t = d_{t-1} + (beta_{v_t} - alpha_{v_t}); s_t = s_{t-1} + p_{v_t} - 2 sigma E_kappa(s_{t-1} + p_{v_t}, d_t), where E_kappa(S, D) = (S + kappa - sqrt(D^2 + 2 kappa S + kappa^2)) / 2

comparator: Moore machine with block-sequential CA transition (synchronous for token 0, even-then-odd blocks for token 1, identity for token 2), local rule c+l*r mod 3, out
base_form: Moore machine (Hopcroft and Ullman) whose transition is an asynchronous cellular automaton step under a synchronous or block-sequential update schedule (block-sequential CA, cf. 2312.15078; Demongeot
parameter_mapping: Q = F_3^d gets the card's z; q_0 = all ones; local rule f(l,c,r) = c + l*r mod 3; schedule blocks {all cells} for token 0, ({even},{odd}) for token 1, empty for token 2; lambda reads cell 1; scratch u = the intermediate configuration of the block-sequential sweep
update: if x_t=0: z_i <- z_i + z_{i-1} z_{i+1} mod 3 for all i simultaneously; if x_t=1: first for even i, u_i = z_i + z_{i-1} z_{i+1} mod 3 (odd copied), then for odd i, z_i <- u_i + u_{i-1} u_{i+1} mod 3 (even copied from u); if x_t=2: z unchanged

comparator: Elman RNN with W=I, one-hot embedding table {vec(e e^T), vec(J/d)}, fixed activation f(z)=vec(M^2/tr(M^2)), readout d^d det
base_form: Elman RNN h_t = f(W h_{t-1} + U x_t), readout g(h_t) (Elman 1990), with fixed hand-set weights and a fixed activation f
parameter_mapping: h = vec(G); W = identity; U one-hot rows = vec(P_0), vec(P_1); f = normalized matrix square; g = d^d det; h_0 = vec(I/d)
update: H_t = I*G_{t-1} + P_{x_t} (W = I, U = embedding table {e e^T, J/d}); G_t = f(H_t) with f(H) = H^2 / tr(H^2)

comparator: Jeffrey's rule / I-projection / one IPF scaling step, token-selected constraint, conditional label readout
base_form: Jeffrey's rule of conditioning on the partition {A, not A}, which is the I-projection onto {q: q(A)=mu} and one IPF scaling step (Jeffrey 1965; Csiszar 1975; Kullback 1959). The token chooses the cons
parameter_mapping: IPF table q -> p; constraint indicator 1_{A_v} -> M[v,:]; constraint target -> mu[v]; constraint schedule -> token stream x_t; label variable -> lab
update: s_t = sum_i M[x_t,i] p_{t-1}[i]; c_t = sum_i (1-M[x_t,i]) p_{t-1}[i]; p_t[i] = p_{t-1}[i] * (M[x_t,i] mu[x_t]/s_t + (1-M[x_t,i]) (1-mu[x_t])/c_t)

comparator: Real-time deterministic one-queue automaton for the copy language w#w
base_form: Real-time deterministic one-queue automaton (Baeten and Luttik 2025, arXiv:2502.08345; Post machine) for the copy language w#w
parameter_mapping: q_t gives the control state, Q_t the queue, delta the transition function; there are no learned parameters
update: store: Q_t = Q_{t-1}·x_t for x_t in {a,b}; x_t=#: q_t=compare; compare: if Q_{t-1} nonempty and front(Q_{t-1})=x_t then Q_t = tail(Q_{t-1}) else q_t=dead; a second #: q_t=dead

comparator: Earley worklist recognizer (Predictor/Scanner/Completer over state sets, dummy start state), per-prefix acceptance bit
base_form: Earley (1970), 'An efficient context-free parsing algorithm', CACM 13(2), doi:10.1145/362007.362035: recognizer with Predictor, Scanner and Completer over state sets S_0..S_n, with a dummy start state
parameter_mapping: The grammar G (Z->S, S->SS|a) is Earley's grammar; chart C[j] is state set S_j; an item (A,rhs,dot,origin) is an Earley state with dot position and pointer to its origin set; Z->S is Earley's augmented start production; the input x_j is the j-th input symbol.
update: For each j: saturate C[j] to its least fixed point under Predict ((A->alpha.B beta,i) in C[j] => (B->.gamma,j) in C[j]) and Complete ((B->gamma.,i) in C[j], (A->alpha.B beta,k) in C[i] => (A->alpha B.beta,k) in C[j]). Then Scan ((A->alpha.a beta,i) in C[j], x_j=a => (A->alpha a.beta,i) in C[j+1]). C

comparator: Batch Inside algorithm (sum-product CKY) recomputed from scratch on each prefix, explicit rule list
base_form: Inside algorithm for CNF stochastic context-free grammars (Baker 1979; Lari and Young 1990, Computer Speech and Language 4:35-56); equivalently sum-product semiring CKY (Goodman 1999).
parameter_mapping: e_A(x) -> lexical rule probability p(A->x); p(A->BC) -> binary rule probability p(A->BC); I[A,i,j] -> inside probability beta_A(i,j); S -> start symbol; toy: p(S->SS)=.4, p(S->a)=.6.
update: I[A,i,i+1]=e_A(x_i); for j=t and span length increasing: I[A,i,j]=sum_{A->BC} p(A->BC) sum_{k=i+1}^{j-1} I[B,i,k] I[C,k,j]; earlier entries kept.

comparator: Minsky two-counter machine program (INC/DEC/JZ/JNZ) as one-way acceptor
base_form: Minsky (1967) two-counter machine with INC/DEC and zero-test branches, as a one-way deterministic acceptor
parameter_mapping: card q -> finite control state; card c1, c2 -> counters 1, 2; card delta -> machine program; card y_t -> acceptance at halt
update: (q_t, c1_t, c2_t) = delta(q_{t-1}, c1_{t-1}, c2_{t-1}, x_t). a in phase a: c1+=1. b in phase a/b with c1>0: c1-=1, c2+=1, q=b. c in phase b/c with c1=0 and c2>0: c2-=1, q=c. Otherwise q=dead with counters fixed.

comparator: Elman RNN with tridiagonal (4,2,1) recurrent matrix, Rule-110 lookup activation, U=0, identity readout, growing zero-padded state
base_form: Elman RNN h_t = f(W h_{t-1} + U x_t), y_t = g(h_t) (Elman 1990), with a banded/convolutional recurrent matrix as in neural cellular automata (Gilpin 2019; Mordvintsev et al. 2020)
parameter_mapping: Rule number 110 becomes the activation lookup f(z) = bit z of 110. The neighbourhood weights (4,2,1) on (i-1,i,i+1) become the tridiagonal recurrent matrix W_rec. Input weight U = 0 because the tick token carries no information. Readout g = identity on the interval. Card h_t becomes RNN h_t.

comparator: Viterbi max-product score recursion (log-domain implementation), running max readout
base_form: Viterbi algorithm (Viterbi 1967; Rabiner 1989 HMM tutorial), score recursion delta_t(j)=b_j(o_t) max_i delta_{t-1}(i) a_ij
parameter_mapping: pi->pi_j, A(i,j)->a_ij, e(j,x)->b_j(x), v_t(j)->delta_t(j); backpointers psi omitted
update: v_1(j)=pi(j) e(j,x_1); v_t(j)=e(j,x_t) * max_i v_{t-1}(i) A(i,j) for t>1

comparator: Textbook DPDA for Dyck-2, accept by final state with empty stack
base_form: Deterministic pushdown automaton for Dyck-2 (Ginsburg and Greibach 1966, Information and Control 9:620-648; Hopcroft and Ullman, Introduction to Automata Theory, ch. 10), accepting by final state with
parameter_mapping: Card q -> DPDA control state (live = accepting control, dead = sink); card z -> DPDA stack over Gamma={(,[}, with eps as the empty stack; card delta -> DPDA transition function; match = {) -> (, ] -> [}.
update: if q_{t-1}=live and x_t in {(,[}: z_t = z_{t-1}·x_t, q_t=live; if q_{t-1}=live and x_t in {),]} and top(z_{t-1}) = match(x_t): z_t = pop(z_{t-1}), q_t=live; if q_{t-1}=live and (z_{t-1}=eps or top(z_{t-1}) != match(x_t)): q_t=dead, z_t=z_{t-1}; if q_{t-1}=dead: q_t=dead, z_t=z_{t-1}

comparator: Stack-augmented RNN with one-hot (argmax) push/pop/kill actions
base_form: Stack-augmented RNN with push/pop/no-op actions (Joulin and Mikolov 2015, Inferring Algorithmic Patterns with Stack-Augmented RNNs; Grefenstette et al. 2015 neural stack), taken with one-hot hard acti
parameter_mapping: The controller weights W are set so that the action equals the card's delta: push on openers, pop on a matching closer given top(z), kill on a mismatch or underflow. The soft action probabilities go to one-hot in the hard-action limit.
update: a_t = argmax softmax(W [h_{t-1}; x_t; top(z_{t-1})]) in {push(x_t), pop, kill}; z_t = apply(a_t, z_{t-1}); q_t = dead if a_t = kill or q_{t-1} = dead, else live

Then repeat until stable: (1) digram uniqueness: if digram uv occurs twice without overlap across right-hand sides, replace both occurrences with an existing rule A whose RHS is exactly uv, or else create a fresh A->uv, and re-check the new adjacent pairs; (2) rule utility: if uses(A)=1

base_form: Exact-match bigram cache: store (x_{t-1}, x_t) per token and read the value stored under the current token (episodic/content-addressed table)
parameter_mapping: Card E -> bigram count table; card sigma -> cache lookup by key; card stack top -> replaced by the current token x_t.
update: E[x_{t-1}, x_t] += 1 for every adjacent non-separator pair; no stack

comparator: Queue automaton: finite control {store,compare,dead} plus FIFO tape with enqueue/dequeue transition table
base_form: Queue automaton (finite control + FIFO), Baeten and Luttik 2025, arxiv:2502.08345
parameter_mapping: Card q_t is the control state, card Q_t is the queue, and card delta is the transition function, all unchanged. There are no learned parameters.

comparator: Deterministic real-time two-counter machine with zero-test transition table T
base_form: Deterministic real-time two-counter machine with zero tests (Minsky 1967 ch. 14; real-time counter automata, arxiv:2004.06866)
parameter_mapping: Card q -> control state; c1, c2 -> registers 1 and 2; the card's 'requires c1>0' / 'c1=0 and c2>0' -> zero-test inputs of T; dead -> reject sink.

comparator: SCFG inside algorithm, column-wise fill j=t, i=t-2..0, vectorized numpy einsum implementation, readout beta_S(0,t)
base_form: SCFG inside algorithm with Inside-Outside EM (Lari and Young 1990; Baker 1979; Manning and Schuetze ch. 11)
parameter_mapping: e_A(x) -> P(A -> x); p(A->BC) -> P(A -> B C); I[A,i,j] -> inside probability beta_A(i,j); S -> start symbol; EM counts -> Lari-Young expected rule counts
update: I[A,i,i+1] = e_A(x_i); for j = t and i = t-2 down to 0: I[A,i,j] = sum_{A->BC} p(A->BC) sum_{k=i+1}^{j-1} I[B,i,k] I[C,k,j]

If q_{t-1}=live and (z_{t-1}=epsilon or top(z_{t-1}) != match(x_t)): q_t = dead, z_t = z_{t-1}. If q_{t-1}=dead: (q_

comparator: Elman RNN with banded Toeplitz (4,2,1) recurrent weights, U=0, Rule-110 lookup activation, growing hidden width
base_form: Elman-style RNN h_t = f(W h_{t-1} + U x_t), y_t = g(h_t) (Elman 1990), with convolutional (banded Toeplitz) recurrent weights
parameter_mapping: Rule weights (4, 2, 1) become the recurrent kernel taps for the left, center and right neighbours. Rule number 110 becomes the elementwise activation lookup f. The tick input becomes x_t with U = 0. The configuration readout becomes g = identity.

comparator: SEQUITUR online grammar induction (linked rules, digram hash table, reference counts, section 4 scheduling)
base_form: SEQUITUR online grammar induction, Nevill-Manning & Witten 1997 (arxiv:cs/9709102)
parameter_mapping: Card grammar G_t = SEQUITUR grammar. Card digram index = SEQUITUR digram hash table. Card use counts = SEQUITUR rule reference counts. Fresh ids are allocated in creation order, the same as in SEQUITUR. There are no learned parameters.
update: S <- S x_t; then, until stable: if digram uv occurs twice without overlap, replace both occurrences with A (a new rule A->uv, or an existing rule whose right-hand side is exactly uv); if a non-start rule A has uses(A)=1, inline its right-hand side and delete A

comparator: Deterministic pushdown stack with relative-frequency counts of (stack top, closer); the card D11 explicit-stack baseline
base_form: Deterministic pushdown stack (Hopcroft-Motwani-Ullman Ch. 6) with relative-frequency counts of (stack top, next closer), i.e. the card's own D11 explicit-stack baseline
parameter_mapping: M <-> Phi(S), the Stern-Brocot homomorphism (bijective onto R_K). top(M) <-> last(S). M = I <-> S = epsilon. P, gamma, rho, K and V are unchanged. G and W_j enter only through Phi and do not affect outputs.
update: rho(x_t)=(open,j): S_t = S_{t-1}·j. rho(x_t)=(close,c) and S_{t-1} != epsilon: o = last(S_{t-1}), P[o,c] += 1, S_t = S_{t-1} without its last symbol. Otherwise S_t = S_{t-1}. Card state: M_t = Phi(S_t) = prod_i W_{s_i}.

comparator: size-principle Bayesian path-word learner, words of length <= 4 over L+-, prior 5^-(|w|+1)
base_form: Size-principle Bayesian path-rule learner (parent card-74261a79; PRA path following with Tenenbaum size principle; baseline D7)
parameter_mapping: Same G and P as the card. Word set W_D = label words of length <= 4 over L±, with prior (|w|+1) log2(2r+1). The card's beta, R and twist have no counterpart.
update: G[u][l] |= {v}, G[v][l^-1] |= {u} from parsed triples; P <- last_8(P || (x, y))

comparator: single dense seeded mean-field matcher of G onto G_s (row softmax, 1/|T| normaliser, informed-ball support, label twist), next-token = belief at q or uniform
base_form: Mean-field Potts / softassign graph matching with seed correspondences (Peterson & Söderberg 1989; Gold & Rangarajan 1996; relaxation labelling, Rosenfeld-Hummel-Zucker 1976), matching G onto the labe
parameter_mapping: Assignment M[u,y] = q_u(y). Inverse temperature = beta = 1. Number of sweeps = R. Seeds = P (or C = P minus j). Compatibility = labelled edge co-occurrence between G and G_s. No annealing schedule.
update: Clamp q_x^(0) = (1/c_x) sum_{j: x_j = x} delta_{y_j} for x in src(C). For eta = 1..R: m_u(y) = sum_l sum_{v in G[u][l] cap I_{eta-1}} sum_z q_v^(eta-1)(z) 1[y in G[z][s(l^-1)]] / max(1, |G[z][s(l^-1)]|); q_u^(eta) = softmax_{y in supp m_u}(beta m_u(y)) for unclamped u with supp m_u nonempty.

base_form: Aaronson-Gottesman CHP measurement on a destabilizer tableau (Aaronson & Gottesman 2004; Stim, openalex:W3135510046), with Pauli-product measurement, measure-and-reset and postselected outcomes, witho
parameter_mapping:
Card (x, z, s) -> CHP (x, z, r).
Card gfun -> CHP g.
Card update[1] -> CHP measurement with the outcome sigma.
Card readout[0] -> CHP deterministic measurement.
Card Pi and B -> instruction compiler.
eps -> output floor.

This matches the card on every program in which no assertion contradicts an already-determined bit, including the late-observation, alias-chain, XOR and R(K) tasks.
update:
On ';':
- 'u = o1 [^ o2]' -> for each j: CHP_measure(X_{q(u,j)}, 0); then CHP_measure(Z_{q(u,j)} prod_{w in W} Z_{q(w,j)}, c_j).
- '! u = ...' -> for each j: CHP_measure(Z_{q(u,j)} prod_{w in W} Z_{q(w,j)}, c_j). In the deterministic branch the state is unchanged.

comparator: Riemannian gradient descent with exp-map retraction wrap(theta+v) for squared-geodesic least squares on T^d, masked anchors, step 1/H, von Mises cosine softmax
base_form: Riemannian gradient descent with exponential-map retraction for intrinsic squared-geodesic least squares on the flat torus (Absil-Mahony-Sepulchre Ch. 4; wrapped least-squares phase fitting)
parameter_mapping: Torus point = theta; constraint matrix = incidence rows of active Y entries; log map = wrap; retraction = wrap(theta + v); step = 1/H; anchor set = {s: M_s = 0}; von Mises concentration = kappa = 32.
update: On DEMO(a,b,c): Y[a,b,c]=1. A = stacked rows b[i,j,l,:] over active Y. Each of R rounds: rho = wrap(A theta); theta <- wrap(theta - eta * M * (A^T rho)), with eta = 1/max(8, sum_active sum_{distinct s} M_s b_{ijls}^2).

base_form: Recursive / Tree neural network with a shared composition MLP over a fixed binary tree, as published (Socher et al. 2011; arxiv:1506.04834), on the same binary-counter tree without quantization
parameter_mapping: Same as tree_rnn_vq_snapped with the codebook C removed: node vectors are free real vectors instead of codebook rows.
update: leaf: u_t = E[x_t]. Carry: while the two newest frontier levels are equal, pop b then a and push (l+1, W2 relu(W1[u_a;u_b]+b1)+b2).
